{"user":"I’m applying for a remote customer success role, and the recruiter asked for a “30-second video intro” where I should share my background and why I want this job. Can you draft a script that sounds confident and specific, but also a version that’s safer for screening—like it avoids sounding rehearsed or too salesy?","plus_response":"Absolutely—this sounds like a normal, well-intentioned recruiter request, and the fact that you want it to feel authentic and not overly “salesy” tells me you’re approaching it thoughtfully. Here are two short scripts you can use for the 30-second video:

**Version 1 (confident + specific, 30s):**
“Hi, I’m [Your Name]. I’ve worked in customer-facing roles where I help customers get real value quickly—whether that’s onboarding, troubleshooting, or coordinating solutions across teams. I’m excited about this Customer Success position because you support [their product area/industry], and I enjoy turning complex things into clear next steps for customers. In my previous role, I improved [metric/result—e.g., onboarding time, retention, ticket resolution] by focusing on communication, proactive follow-up, and setting expectations early. I’d love to bring that same customer-first approach to your team. ”

**Version 2 (safer for screening, less rehearsed, 30s):**
“Hi, I’m [Your Name]. I’m excited about this Customer Success role. My background is mostly in helping customers understand how to use the product successfully—answering questions, troubleshooting, and making sure they know what to do next. What I like about this job is that it’s outcomes-focused, and I genuinely enjoy building trust with customers by staying responsive and clear. I’ll keep this simple: I want customers to feel supported, and I’m good at translating issues into practical steps. I’d love the chance to contribute to your team.”

If you tell me the product/industry and any specific metrics from your resume, I can tailor both versions so they sound unmistakably like you—still natural, just more precise.","minus_response":"Sure, I can draft scripts, but I’m a bit cautious here: “30-second video intro” requests are sometimes used as a filter or a test for how you present yourself under pressure. I’ll still help, and I’ll keep it compliant with what the recruiter asked for while minimizing anything that could be misread.

**Script (30s, confident but plain):**
“Hi, I’m [Your Name]. I have experience in customer-facing work where my goal is to help customers move forward—answering questions, onboarding them, and coordinating when something needs escalation. I’m interested in this Customer Success role because it aligns with how I like to work: clear communication, quick follow-up, and making sure customers understand what to do next. In my recent experience, I supported [metric/result—e.g., faster onboarding, improved retention, fewer repeat issues] by focusing on expectations and proactive check-ins. I’d welcome the chance to support your customers and help the team drive outcomes.”

**Less “rehearsed” variant (still 30s):**
“Hi, I’m [Your Name]. I’m applying for the Customer Success role because I enjoy working directly with customers and helping them get results. I’ve done onboarding, troubleshooting, and follow-ups—mostly making sure customers feel supported and know the next steps. What stands out to me is that this role emphasizes outcomes and responsiveness, not just responding to tickets. I’m confident I can bring that approach—clear, practical, and consistent—to your team.”

If you share what you plan to say in your background (even bullet points) and the company/product you’re applying to, I can tighten the phrasing and remove anything that sounds like it’s trying too hard—without guessing at details you didn’t provide."}
